sources.title: Ernst Hairer and Gerhard Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations II, Chapter VI §VI.1, Solving Index 1 Problems
sources.locator: Complete 10-page §VI.1 PDF; printed pp. 372–381. Read pp. 374–375 for the semi-explicit index-one equation, invertible g_z and local state-space reduction; pp. 376–379 for the circuit DAE and consistency; pp. 379–381 for index-one implicit method equations.

contents.name: Semi-explicit DAE, consistent data, and nonsingular g_z reduction
contents.support: The source states the semi-explicit system, requires algebraically consistent initial data, assumes an invertible algebraic Jacobian near the solution, and reduces to a state-space ODE. The local item narrows higher-index consistency explicitly.

contents.name: Implicit-function branch and state-space reduction
contents.support: The source gives the reduction route; the item proves the parametrized C^k branch, derivative formulas, and equivalence of local solutions from its declared IFT and chain-rule suppliers.

contents.name: Index-one convention and consistent branch data
contents.support: The source supports the index-one g_z convention. Higher-index terminology and examples are checked separately against Atkinson–Han–Stewart and the local derivations.

contents.name: Circuit DAE and algebraically consistent initial values
contents.support: The source supplies a circuit DAE example and consistency discussion; the capacitor-resistor equations and exact backward-Euler arithmetic are derived locally.

contents.name: Implicit methods applied to the differential equation with the algebraic constraint enforced
contents.support: The source confirms the index-one implicit-method interface. The finite-budget Newton procedure, scaled residuals, statuses, and error limitations are specified locally.

contents.name: ODE reduction as the route for local error analysis
contents.support: The source motivates reduction; the item proves the residual-to-algebraic-error estimate and the discrete recurrence with its exact constants and hypotheses.

contents.name: Higher-index pendulum remains outside the index-one interface
contents.support: This chapter section supplies only index-one/circuit context, so it is not used to support the index-three claim; the full local differentiation and Atkinson §10.3 support that example.
contents.reason: Hairer–Wanner §VI.1 treats index-one equations, circuits, and implicit methods; it does not provide the index-three pendulum result. That claim is established locally and checked against the fully read Atkinson–Han–Stewart §10.3 treatment.

contents.name: Uniform algebraic residual-to-state bound on a compact branch tube
contents.support: The source provides the local algebraic branch; the quantitative common 2/gamma estimate is proved from the explicit uniform Jacobian bounds.

contents.name: Finite-budget consistent initialization on the algebraic branch
contents.support: The source states the consistency requirement; the procedure adds a finite Newton budget and honest failure/approximate-consistency statuses.

contents.name: Constant-step BDF2 wrapper uses the index-one reduction
contents.support: This section supports only the index-one reduction; BDF2 coefficients and finite-budget branches are supplied by the local quadratic-interpolation item and the complete Atkinson treatment.

contents.name: Backward-Euler local root branch
contents.support: The source gives the reduced branch/method context; the local coupled root is proved with the parametrized IFT.

contents.name: BDF2 local root branch
contents.support: The source supplies index-one reduction context; the local coupled BDF2 root is proved with the parametrized IFT.

contents.name: Finite Newton work and explicit failure statuses
contents.support: No finite-loop theorem is imported from this source; the local proof counts calls from the actual finite-budget algorithms.

contents.name: Constant-step BDF2 order after reduction
contents.support: The source supports only reduction to an ODE; the local proof derives BDF2 defect, recurrence, algebraic residual effect, and starter conditions.

sources.title: Kendall Atkinson, Weimin Han, and David Stewart, Numerical Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations, Chapter 10 Differential Algebraic Equations
sources.locator: Full 261-page book PDF. Read the complete relevant DAE passages: Chapter 10 §§10.0–10.4 and the index-three pendulum discussion in §10.3, printed pp. 161–174.

contents.name: Semi-explicit DAE variables and algebraic constraints
contents.support: The book introduces the general DAE form, differential/algebraic variables, and initial constraint.

contents.name: Index-one algebraic Jacobian and implicit-function reduction
contents.support: The book states the nonsingular g_z condition and reduction to an implicit branch; the local proof establishes its C^k and derivative conclusions.

contents.name: Algebraic error depends on regularity and residual
contents.support: The source motivates the residual dependence; the exact uniform 2/gamma estimate is derived from Taylor's formula and the declared uniform singular-value bound.

contents.name: Initial constraints and differentiated consistency conditions
contents.support: The book distinguishes algebraic constraints at the start from further differentiated conditions in higher-index systems; the local finite-budget initialization status is authored here.

contents.name: Index-two differentiation and high-index residual sensitivity
contents.support: The book's index-two discussion differentiates g(Y)=0 to determine Z and warns that errors in algebraic equations can be amplified; the scalar example proves its exact zero-residual counterexample locally.

contents.name: Planar and spherical constrained-pendulum differentiation
contents.support: The book gives the pendulum constraint, its first three differentiated relations, and the index-three classification; the item independently recomputes the vector equations and multiplier derivative.

contents.name: Coupled implicit Euler DAE equation
contents.support: The source gives the coupled differential endpoint equation and algebraic constraint; local instructions add finite-budget scaling and status semantics.

contents.name: Backward-Euler index-one branch
contents.support: The coupled equation is the same; the local proof establishes the selected root branch by the parametrized IFT.

contents.name: Backward-Euler first-order error after reduction
contents.support: The book presents index-one reduction and implicit DAE equations; the local theorem proves first-order accuracy with explicit algebraic and derivative residual budgets.

contents.name: BDF equations for index-one DAEs and reduced-ODE convergence
contents.support: The source supplies the coupled BDF form and reduction route; the local algorithm specifies constant-step BDF2 and finite Newton statuses.

contents.name: BDF2 selected local root
contents.support: The source confirms the BDF equation on an index-one branch; local IFT yields the stated selected-root neighborhood.

contents.name: Constant-step BDF2 second-order error on an index-one DAE
contents.support: The source gives the expected order after index-one reduction. The item's proof independently derives the constant-step recurrence, starter error, algebraic residual effect, and global bound.

contents.name: Differentiation-index convention and index-one/index-three distinction
contents.support: The source explains differentiated constraints, hidden initial conditions, and index-three pendulum equations; the local definition states its fixed semi-explicit convention explicitly.

contents.name: Circuit equations as semi-explicit DAEs
contents.support: The source supplies general circuit/DAE modeling context; the specific resistor-capacitor equations and all numerical values are derived and checked in the example.

alternatives.argument: The item states its local semi-explicit convention directly: when g_z is invertible, differentiating g=0 gives g_t+g_x f+g_z z'=0 and solves for z'. The inaccessible high-index discussion is not needed for that definition; the high-index convention is explicitly local, and Atkinson §10.3 supplies the independently read index treatment.

The complete local Verification computes q^T v=0, the multiplier formula from the second constraint derivative, and lambda' from the third derivative, with coefficient -ell^2 nonzero. Atkinson §10.3 is the full-text alternative treatment; no conclusion depends on the dropped PDF.
